=={{header|Omegese}}==
{{works with|omc|sha256 2c824805, aien-dev/omega-mv e5b32567, Linux AArch64}}
Omega has no imports, so the small output helpers (<code>emit</code> and friends) are part of the program.
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
om2
text nl "\n"
text sp " "
text first "first 10 terms:"
text th "the 1000th term: "
text fl "terms up to the 100000th that are less than the term before: "
note q n is Q(n) for n = 1..100000; Q(n) < n here, so every index n - Q(n-1) and n - Q(n-2) is in range
global q ulong 100001
note emit writes every byte of a to stdout; a short write is retried, an error exits 1
fn emit a view uchar * to void
o = ulong 0
while lt o len a bound 4096
k = write 1 a o sub len a o
if le k 0
exit 1
end
o = add o ulong k
end
end
note emitu writes n in decimal; 20 digits hold every ulong
fn emitu n ulong to void
d = new uchar 20 0
i = ulong 20
v = n
while true bound 20
i = sub i 1
put d i uchar add rem v 10 48
v = div v 10
if eq v 0
break
end
end
emit part d i sub 20 i
end
fn main to int
put q 1 1
put q 2 1
for i ulong 99998
n = add i 3
a = get q sub n get q sub n 1
b = get q sub n get q sub n 2
put q n add a b
end
emit first
for i ulong 10
emit sp
emitu get q add i 1
end
emit nl
emit th
emitu get q 1000
emit nl
c = ulong 0
for i ulong 99999
n = add i 2
if lt get q n get q sub n 1
c = add c 1
end
end
emit fl
emitu c
emit nl
ret 0
end
</syntaxhighlight>
{{out}}
<pre>
first 10 terms: 1 1 2 3 3 4 5 5 6 6
the 1000th term: 502
terms up to the 100000th that are less than the term before: 49798
</pre>
